fullDescription: A multi-step business account application form whose whole idea is that it only asks you what it could not look up. Every question the product already answered is a solid deep-indigo slab carrying the answer plus the source it came from, and the handful it still needs are white boxes with a heavy ink border and a real input, so the dark mass is the work already done and the white gaps are the work left. Flat pale-lilac ground, one grotesque, sentence case throughout, no gradients and no shadows. Reusable for onboarding, KYC, applications, checkout review steps, and any flow that prefills from an API.
prompt:
## Resumo
A full-page web application FORM (a product screen, not a marketing page) for opening a business bank account, on a flat pale-lilac ground #e9e2ff. There is no hero and no headline describing the idea: a 52px masthead strip (small solid square mark, wordmark, a divider, the document title, and a right-side 'Saved 2 minutes ago' state) sits above a thin ink rule, and the page opens straight onto the sheet. Two columns on desktop: a sticky 240px left rail (a #f9f7ff panel with a 1px ink border listing the four blocks with their completion counts, the current one marked by a 3px accent bar) and a 760px sheet. The sheet opens on two left-aligned lines, '11 of 17 answered. 6 questions left.' and, in the accent, 'Every answer we filled in shows where it came from.' Then four blocks of rows. ELEVEN rows are FILLED: solid #12004b slabs, each carrying the question in pale lilac, the answer in white at 18px, a muted-lilac line naming where it came from ('Companies House, matched 12 June', 'HMRC VAT register, checked 12 June', 'Open banking, connected 12 June'), and a small underlined 'Edit' link so the row reads changeable rather than disabled. SIX rows are OPEN: white fill, 2px ink border, a real input affordance (text field, a paired name/email row, a select with a chevron, a textarea, a dashed upload area) and a helper line in the accent stating the actual reason the answer is needed. One open row is rendered in its FOCUSED state: 2px accent border, a 4px accent bar down its left edge, partially typed text and a solid caret block. One filled slab reads 'Proof of address / Not needed. / Your registered address already matched the register' — a question the product deleted rather than asked. The page closes with a one-line data-retention footer and a full-width white action bar with a 2px ink top border: '6 questions left, about 3 minutes' on the left, a 'Save and close' link and a solid accent 'Review and submit' button on the right.

## Estilo Visual
Design a flat, border-defined product form in a STRICT single-hue indigo system: a flat pale-lilac ground #e9e2ff across the whole page, near-black indigo #12004b for type and for the filled row slabs, one hard ultramarine #1f00ab for the primary button, focus states and helper text, #a99ae0 for muted text inside a dark slab, #6f63a8 for placeholders on white, #f9f7ff for the rail panel, white for open input rows. NO other hue anywhere and NO gradient of any kind — flat fills and borders only, no shadows, no blur, no glow, no dot-grid or line-grid background. Use ONE typeface, Inter Tight, at weights 400/500/600 only: block headings 22px/600 with -0.02em tracking, answers 18px/500, labels 13px/500, source and helper lines 12-13px/400, buttons and links 14px/500. Everything is SENTENCE CASE: never use text-transform uppercase with letter-spacing anywhere on the page. 4px radius on every box, input and button. Pure CSS, no JavaScript.

## Layout e Estrutura

### Masthead strip
A 52px strip on the ground colour with a 1px ink rule under it. Left: a 20px solid ink square mark, the wordmark at 16px/600, a short vertical divider, then the document title at 15px/400 ('Business account application'). Right: a muted 13px save state ('Saved 2 minutes ago'). No nav links, no pill CTA, no centred logo.

### Sticky block rail
A 240px panel in #f9f7ff with a 1px ink border and 4px radius, sticky to the top of the viewport on desktop. Inside, the four block names with their completion counts in sentence case at 14px ('The business 6/8', 'People 3/4', 'Money 1/3', 'Documents 1/2'). The current block is full-strength ink with a 3px accent bar on its left edge; the others are ink at 60% opacity. On mobile it stacks above the sheet as a compact list.

### Sheet header
Two left-aligned lines directly above the first block, no hero and no display type. First, the count at 20px/500 in ink ('11 of 17 answered. 6 questions left.'). Second, the page's one claim at 14px/400 in the accent ('Every answer we filled in shows where it came from.'). Every number stated here must agree with the rail counts and the action bar.

### Filled row (the product already knows this)
A solid #12004b block, 4px radius, 18px 20px padding, laid out as a left stack plus a right link. Left: the question at 13px/500 in pale lilac #e9e2ff, the answer at 18px/500 in white, and the source at 12px/400 in muted lilac #a99ae0 naming exactly where the value came from and when. Right: a small underlined 'Edit' link at 13px/500 in pale lilac, so the row reads changeable rather than disabled. Build eleven of these. Every one must carry a source line — that is the page's claim, and it has to be literally true.

### Open row (we still need this from you)
A white block with a 2px #12004b border, 4px radius, 18px 20px padding: the label at 13px/500 in ink, then a real input affordance 40px tall with a 1px ink border, 4px radius and a placeholder in #6f63a8, then a helper line at 13px/400 in the accent that states the actual reason the answer is needed rather than a generic hint. Variants: a plain text field, a pair of side-by-side name and email fields with a small 'Add another' ghost link, a select showing 'Choose a range' with a plain chevron, a three-line textarea, and an 88px dashed-border upload area reading 'Drop a PDF here or choose a file'. Build six of these and no more.

### Focused row (freeze the interaction into the static render)
Take one open row and render it in its focused state so a still capture shows the form being used: the box border becomes 2px in the accent, a 4px accent bar runs down its left edge, and the field contains partially typed text followed by a solid 2px-wide accent caret block.

### The deleted question
One filled slab whose answer is that there is nothing to ask: the question 'Proof of address', the answer 'Not needed.', and the source line 'Your registered address already matched the register'. Style it exactly like the other filled slabs. This row is the design's argument — a question the product removed rather than asked.

### Action bar
A full-width white bar with a 2px ink top border at the end of the page. Left: '6 questions left, about 3 minutes' at 14px in ink. Right: an underlined 'Save and close' link and a solid accent primary button, 44px tall, white 15px/500 text, 4px radius, reading 'Review and submit'. Keep this a plain, obvious, high-contrast affordance in the ordinary place — never fold the primary action into the design's conceit. On mobile the button goes full width.

## Componentes Especiais de UI

### Provenance row — A pre-filled answer rendered as a solid ink slab whose third line names the register or connection the value came from and when it was checked.
Render a pre-filled form answer as a solid near-black indigo slab rather than a greyed-out disabled input. Three stacked lines: the question in pale lilac at 13px, the answer in white at 18px, and the source in muted lilac at 12px naming the specific register and date ('Companies House, matched 12 June', 'HMRC VAT register, checked 12 June', 'Open banking, connected 12 June', 'Your document upload'). A small underlined 'Edit' link sits at the top right so the value reads changeable. Never write a generic source like 'auto-filled' — name the actual system and the date, because the differentiated source line is what makes the page's claim real rather than asserted.

### Open input row — The counterpart to the provenance row: a white, heavily bordered box marking a question the product could not answer for you.
Render a question that still needs a human answer as a white box with a 2px near-black indigo border, so it reads as a hole punched in the dark stack of answered rows. Inside: a 13px label, a real 40px input with a 1px border and a muted placeholder, and a helper line in the accent colour that gives the actual reason this one is being asked ('We're asking because your year end was 31 March and nothing has been filed since'). The visual contrast between these white boxes and the solid slabs is the entire design, so never soften it with a tint, a shadow or a lighter border.

### Block completion rail — A sticky panel listing each block of the form with how many of its questions are already answered.
A sticky side panel on a slightly lighter tint of the ground with a 1px ink border, listing each block of the form in sentence case with a completion count ('The business 6/8'). Mark the current block with a 3px accent bar on its left edge and full-strength ink; dim the others to 60%. The counts must sum to the totals stated in the sheet header and the action bar. On mobile, stack it above the sheet as a compact list rather than hiding it.

### Deleted-question slab — A filled row whose answer is that the question no longer applies, styled identically to the answered rows.
Render one row where the product removed the requirement instead of satisfying it: the question, the answer 'Not needed.', and a source line explaining why ('Your registered address already matched the register'). Style it exactly like every other answered slab so it reads as work completed, not as an empty state.

### Reason-giving helper text — Helper copy under each open input that states why the product needs this specific answer.
Under every input the user still has to fill, write one accent-coloured line at 13px giving the real reason it is being asked, in plain sentences and never in marketing voice: 'A range is fine. We use it to set your daily limits, not to judge the application.' / 'Only the people you want to give a card to. You can change this later.' / 'Only if you trade under a different name to the legal one. Leave it blank if you don't.' Tie every constraint to a named state rather than a printed number, so nothing on the page can contradict anything else.
